tasks.short: Install and operate the recording equipment.

steps.what: Show the equipment list assigned to this room.
Install, adjust, and operate electronic equipment to record and transmit.
Set aside a unit that will not record or transmit.

tasks.design: The {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the equipment list already assigned to the room. The audio technician installs, adjusts, and operates that equipment to record and transmit. A unit that will not run is set aside by the technician. The list does not install anything. A room with no list leaves the screen blank.
tasks.previous_blocker: The list was a van sheet, and a missing cable was discovered after the audience was seated.
tasks.enabler_now: The room list can be shown before the cases are opened. The install itself is unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: Cables, gain, and a picture that actually leaves the room still depend on the technician's hands.
tasks.human_edge: The technician installs and operates the equipment. The list only says what was assigned.
tasks.altitude: Install and operation stay physical. The room list is visible first, and a unit that fails is still set aside by the technician.

reach.task: Place equipment in a room they have already drawn.
reach.learn: The drawing does not put the case on the floor.

evidence.claim: An equipment list names what was assigned to the room. It does not install, adjust, or operate that equipment.
Setting a failed unit aside is the technician's decision after trying it. The list cannot know the failure.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.
Fields: The room id and the equipment list if one is already assigned. The list is not created here. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the list from the operations system already used for the room before making a new inventory.
unknowns: Whether conferencing, radio, and television jobs share one equipment list or three.
research_questions: Who may substitute a different model when the assigned unit fails?

already_counted.description: Installing, operating, and setting a failed unit aside stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Correct the room list when a substituted unit stays in the room.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Installing, adjusting, and operating the equipment stays with the technician. Only opening a room list that already exists is removed. A room with no list saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Control lights and sound at the event.

steps.what: Show the cue list already written for this event.
Control the lights and sound during the performance and the intermission.
Mark a cue that failed before or after the concert.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the cue list already written for the event. The audio technician controls the lights and the sound before, during, and after the performance, including the intermission. A cue that fails is marked by the technician. The list does not move a fader. An event with no cue list leaves the screen blank and the desk is run from the paper copy.
tasks.previous_blocker: The cue list was a marked script, and a failed cue was remembered rather than marked.
tasks.enabler_now: The written cue list can be on screen. Running the desk during the event cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A level that is right on the list can still be wrong for the room and the crowd.
tasks.human_edge: The technician runs the lights and the sound. The cue list is the plan, not the show.
tasks.altitude: The desk stays with the technician for the whole event. The cue list is visible, and a failed cue is still marked by hand.

reach.task: Play a concert while someone else runs the desk.
reach.learn: The cue list does not replace the person at the desk.

evidence.claim: A cue list already written can be displayed. Displaying it does not control lights or sound.
Marking a failed cue is the technician's note after hearing the room. The list does not detect the failure.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.
Fields: The event id and the cue list if one is already written. The cues are not composed here. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the cue list from the document store before building a new cue tool.
unknowns: Whether concerts and conferences share one cue format.
research_questions: Who writes the cue list, the technician or the stage manager?

already_counted.description: Running the lights and sound, and marking a failed cue, stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Drop cue lists for events that have already closed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still controls lights and sound for the whole event. Only showing a cue list that was already written is removed. An event with no list saves nothing of the desk time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show which video source is currently live.
Switch sources of video input from one camera or studio to another.
Hold a source that is not the called programming.

tasks.design: The {OPS_SYSTEM} shows which video source is live. The audio technician switches the input from one camera or studio to another, including a change from film to live or from network to local programming. A source that was not called is held. The screen does not press the switch. A studio with no live tally leaves that line blank.
tasks.previous_blocker: The tally was a light on the camera, and the called source was a voice in the headset.
tasks.enabler_now: The current live source can be named on screen. The switch itself stays on the desk.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the moment of a cut, and refusing a source that is not the one called, stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician makes the cut. The tally only says what is live now.
tasks.altitude: Switching stays at the desk. The technician can see the live source and still holds any source that was not called.

reach.task: Call a change while play is moving.
reach.learn: A display of the current state is not the call.

evidence.claim: Naming the source that is already live is a tally. It does not switch the video input.
Holding an uncalled source is the technician's refusal. A network or local label does not make that decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The studio id and the live tally if the desk already reports it. The next source is not chosen by the tally. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the tally from the switcher already in the room before adding a second display.
unknowns: Whether film, live, network, and local sources share one tally.
research_questions: Who calls the cut, the director or the technician?

already_counted.description: Switching the source and holding an uncalled source stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Rename a source on the tally when a camera is moved.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still switches every video source and still holds a source that was not called. Only the display of the source already live is removed. The display does not make the cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Label the take with the slate the technician already entered.
Record and edit audio material, such as movie soundtracks.
Keep or discard the take after hearing the recording.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store labels the take with the slate id the technician already entered. The technician records and edits the audio, including movie soundtracks, on the recording equipment. The technician keeps or discards the take after hearing it. The label does not edit the sound. A take with no slate id is not labelled.
tasks.previous_blocker: The slate was written on tape, and a take was kept because nobody had time to hear it back.
tasks.enabler_now: The slate id can label the take. The recording and the edit stay at the equipment.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing whether a soundtrack edit works still takes the technician's ear.
tasks.human_edge: The technician records, edits, and decides which take is kept.
tasks.altitude: Recording and editing stay with the technician. The slate label is copied from the id already entered, and the keep-or-discard decision is unchanged.

reach.task: Hear a read-through before calling the take finished.
reach.learn: A label is not a judgement of the sound.

evidence.claim: Copying a slate id the technician already entered labels the take. It does not record or edit the audio.
Keeping a take is a decision after hearing it. The label cannot make that decision.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.
Fields: The slate id the technician entered. A blank slate stops the label. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Store the label in the document store already used for takes before adding a new library.
unknowns: Whether soundtrack edits are done by this technician or handed to an editor.
research_questions: Which takes must be heard in full before they are kept?

already_counted.description: Recording, editing, and keeping the take stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Drop labels for takes that were discarded.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still records and edits the audio and still keeps or discards the take after hearing it. Only copying a slate id already entered is removed. A take with no slate saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician still installs the equipment, still runs the lights and the sound, and still switches the live source. A cue list or a source name on screen does not operate the show.
reach: Musicians and singers depend on the live mix, and this job learns the mix stays at the desk.
Merchandise displayers set a room before a crowd arrives, and this job learns the install is still physical.
skills_to_grow: Install and operate the equipment rather than trust the room list.
Run lights and sound from the desk during the event.
Switch a live source only when that source is the one called.
role.ambitious_version: The show is still run from the desk. Lists on screen tell the technician what was planned, and the technician still makes the live change.
